newsitem.title: UK: Tesco launches personal finance venture.
newsitem.headline: Tesco launches personal finance venture.

text.p: British supermarket group Tesco Plc's Personal Finance joint venture with Royal Bank of Scotland launched on Wednesday with credit cards and the company said it hoped to offer a full range of products, including mortgages, within a year.
"We're hoping in the next year certainly to have trialled and ideally rolled out nation-wide all the range of products," Tesco Personal Finance chief executive
The Tesco Visa credit card will offer a standard rate of interest of 16.9 percent APR and will earn one loyalty point for customers for every two stg spent anywhere in the world.
It also offers a Christmas bonus of 10 points for every one stg of interest paid during the year.
Tesco increased the returns on its ClubCard Plus account to two points for every one stg spent, doubling previous values.
Tesco said it would have 24-hour telephone banking along with in-store services for people who prefer to bank while they shop, to be launched in the autumn.
It is also testing two travel products, offering currency delivered to your home, and travel insurance.
Sach said the company wanted its financial services "in due course we hope to cater for every aspect of family finances."
Sach said he did not see J. Sainsbury as a rival in financial services, rather established high street players such as banks and building societies.
"The whole (supermarket) sector has something fresh and innovative to bring to financial services," he said.

Sainsbury's joint venture Sainsbury's Bank, which it owns with Bank of Scotland, launched mortgages earlier this week and already has credit cards and savings account facilities. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717
